name: Sensor Calibration Fit
blurb: linear calibration coefficients from two or more readings
intro: Enter raw readings next to what a reference instrument said. Two points give the exact line through them; three or more give the least-squares line y = gain · raw + offset, with the residual at every point so you can see whether a straight line is good enough.

inputs.label: Calibration points
inputs.help: Raw = what the sensor/ADC reports; Reference = the true value from the reference instrument. Engineering notation is fine (4k7, 2.5m).

inputs.label: Fixed-point output scale
inputs.help: The integer result is in reference units × this, e.g. 100 = hundredths of a degree.

examples.title: Thermistor ADC counts against a reference thermometer, 4 points
Load cell: two-point calibration, empty and 1 kg

usage: Give points as a table of {raw, ref} pairs (at least two with different raw values), the unit names as text, one raw reading to convert, and the fixed-point scale and fraction bits. It returns gain and offset (ref = gain × raw + offset), the inverse, R², the residual at every point, the converted reading, and C code with float and integer versions. Use it to turn a bench calibration into firmware constants.
sources: Ordinary least-squares straight line: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, section 4.1.4.1 (linear least squares)
Fixed-point scaling (Q format): rule of thumb, value × 2^bits rounded, product in a wide enough integer
